Objective 
 
To encourage all employees for development of their skills in technical and functional areas. 
To build competency in critical areas as identified by the organization from time to time. To 
engage employees in their desire to meet individual and organizational goals. 
 
Scope 
 
The administration of this policy rests with the HR Department of Ideas2IT Technology Services 
Private Limited and the final interpretation of the same rests with the Management.  
 
Eligibility 
 
 This policy will be applicable to all permanent employees of Ideas2IT Technology Services 
Private Limited.  
 Employees should have served a minimum period of 12 months with the organization. 
 The certification must have business relevance as well as role relevance from a current 
role/career development perspective and must be approved by the Manager / Project 
head. 
 Any fundamental certifications completed will not be eligible for reimbursement (Eg: AWS 
Cloud Practitioner, Azure Fundamental etc.)  
Guidelines 
 
 The certification fee will be reimbursed only for the successful completion of certification. 
  Employees would be liable to serve the organization for one year from the date of 
reimbursement. 
 Employee should get prior approval from reporting manager and management before taking 
up the certification. 
 
Internal 
 Employee should claim the certification reimbursement within 40days from 
the date of completion. 
 
The Process Flow 
 
 An employee willing to pursue a certification shall send an email with complete details of the 
certification program, including the purpose, duration and cost to his/her Manager / Project 
Head for approval. 
 
 After receiving a formal approval from the Manager /Project Head, the employee may 
register to pursue the certification program. 
 
 A communication email must be shared to the HR with the complete details of the 
certification program along with the Manager’s approval. 
 
 The cost of the certification would initially be borne by the employee. 
 
 Upon successful completion of the certification program, the employee shall apply for 
reimbursement along with the receipt of fee payment and certificate of award in the 
intranet portal iassistant. 
 
 The employee must share an email with the invoice and the completion certificate for 
approval to the reporting manager and the HR, post which the Management will approve the 
certification reimbursement and will send it across to the Finance team for further processing.  
 
 Within 1year of certification reimbursement If an employee resigns from the services of the 
organization, he/she shall be liable to refund the entire amount reimbursed under this 
policy. 
 
Effective 
This policy is effective from 16th May 2023. 
Disclaimer: 
The applicability, eligibility of the certification reimbursement may be implemented and/or 
changed by Ideas2IT from time to time at the sole discretion of  Ideas2IT  and  such  implemented  
and/or  changed  shall  become applicable to the employees immediately, upon receipt of notice 
of the same.

I. Policy Brief & Purpose 
Our Employee Code of Conduct policy outlines our expectations regarding employees’ behavior 
towards their colleagues, supervisors and overall organization. The Company strives to 
demonstrate the highest standards of ethical conduct. The company does not grant waivers to its 
conduct, conflict of interest and compliance standards. We promote freedom of expression and 
open communication. The purpose of the Code of conduct is to describe principles of business 
conduct and to provide guidance in ethical decision making. The Company expect all employees to 
follow the code of conduct. They should avoid offending, participating in serious disputes and 
disrupting our workplace. The company also expect them to foster a well-organized, respectful and 
collaborative environment. 
II. Scope 
The Code applies to all employees, contractors and the members of the Board of Directors, which 
for purposes of the Code are referred to as "Employees". Contractors include any consultants, 
suppliers and vendors who are required to have access to company’s confidential, business and 
proprietary information in order to perform their duties. 
III. Compliance  
All employees must protect the company’s legality. Employees should comply with all 
environmental, safety and fair dealing laws. The Company expect employees to be ethical and 
responsible when dealing with the company’s finances, products, partnerships and public image. 
Employees are responsible for knowing and complying with the requirements applicable to work 
activities, including those described in this Code and those described in company guidance 
documents (policies, standards, procedures, bulletins, and manuals).

IV. Adherence to Code of Conduct 
The Company strives to demonstrate the highest standards of ethical conduct. The company does 
not grant waivers to its conduct, conflict of interest and compliance standards. 
V. Fair & Respectful Workplace 
The Company has no tolerance on any kind of discriminatory behavior, harassment or 
victimization. Employees should conform with equal opportunity in all aspects of their work, from 
recruitment and performance evaluation to interpersonal relations. 
The Company is committed to achieving a positive work environment characterized by 
professional, dignified, courteous and respectful conduct – an atmosphere marked by esteem for 
the worth of people, where every colleague and stakeholder is treated fairly and where professional 
views and opinions can be discussed opened and courteously. 
The employees come from a variety of backgrounds, and the Organization places much value on 
this diversity. The employees also operate in a multicultural environment and need to be mindful to 
keep their loyalty to the Company and their adherence to ethical principles above their own 
personal origins, beliefs, opinions, preferences, or habits. They must consider how behaviors 
and/or actions may be perceived by others and be accountable for their own actions. 
a) Disrespect 
Disrespectful behavior in terms of lack of the minimum level of courtesy and dignity in 
interaction with others, or inappropriate conduct, comment or display that either insults, 
denigrates, disparages or humiliates someone or depreciates their value, amounts to a breach 
of ethical principles and may lead to disciplinary actions. Disrespect may also relate to general 
statements or attitudes regarding the diversity of human beings and their worth. It can also 
translate into disrespect for people’s work and for the Organization, its mandate. 
b) Discrimination & Favoritism 
The Organization prohibits discrimination based on gender, race, religion or belief, nationality, 
ethnic or social origin, age, sexual orientation, marital status, disability or other aspects of 
personal status. Discrimination includes actions, made either directly or indirectly, based on 
distinctions or prejudices which have the purpose or effect of treating individuals or groups 
unfairly or unjustly. It may include a series of events or a one-time incident. 
c) Abuse of Authority 
The abuse of authority/power is the improper use of a position of influence, power or authority 
by an individual towards others. This is particularly serious when the alleged offender uses his 
or her influence, power or authority to negatively influence the career or employment conditions 
(including, but not limited to, appointment, assignment, contract renewal, performance 
  
 
evaluation or promotion) of other individuals. Abuse of authority can include a one-time 
incident or a series of incidents. It may also consist of conduct that creates a hostile or offensive 
work environment, which includes, but is not limited to, the use of intimidation, threats, 
blackmail or coercion. Decisions made through the proper use of managerial and supervisory 
responsibilities are not considered as abuse of authority.  
d) Workplace Harassment 
Harassment is an unwanted behavior directed at another identified person.  
Harassment may:  
• Happen between an individual against another individual, either at the same hierarchical 
level or between individuals with different hierarchical levels and/or different contractual 
status. 
• Take the form of bullying, characterized by the underlying perception of an imbalance of 
power, and by the repeated or habitual use of force, physical and/or emotional aggression 
or coercion to intimidate or dominate others. 
• Occur between a group and an individual, in which case it is referred to as “mobbing”. 
Harassment may be obvious, or it may be insidious, and interfere with the recipient’s ability to 
carry out their functions and/or create an intimidating or hostile work environment. Harassment 
can make someone feel anxious, angry, frustrated or humiliated. Harassment may be present 
in the form of words, gestures, or other actions that alarm, threaten, abuse, demean, 
intimidate, belittle, or cause personal humiliation, embarrassment or emotional distress to 
another person. Harassment may not necessarily happen face to face but may also occur in 
written communications, email, phone, and supervision methods. 
e) Sexual Harassment 
The Organization does not tolerate sexual harassment. Sexual harassment is a particularly 
severe form of harassment handled by the Policy on Prevention of Harassment. Sexual 
harassment is understood as any unwelcome, unsolicited and unreciprocated, sexual 
advance, request for sexual favor, verbal or physical conduct or gesture of a sexual nature, or 
any other behavior of a sexual nature (including pornography, sexually colored remarks) that 
has or that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to offend, humiliate or intimidate 
another person. 
Individuals found to have engaged in acts of sexual harassment will be subject to disciplinary 
measures in accordance with The Organization Policy, including being terminated. In severe 
corroborated cases, they may also become the subject of criminal proceedings. 
 
  
 
Complaint Mechanism 
An appropriate complaint mechanism in the form of “Complaints Committee” has been 
created in the Company for time-bound redressal of the complaint made by the victim. 
Complaints Committee 
The Company has instituted a Complaints Committee for redressal of sexual harassment 
complaint (made by the victim) and for ensuring time bound treatment of such complaints. 
Initially, and till further notice, the Complaints Committee will comprise of the following four 
members:  
1. Presiding Officer: Bhavani Kattavur Raman  
2. Gayathri Vivekanandan (Member) 
3. Arun Ganesan (Member) 
4. Sugumar (Member) 
The Presiding Officer reserves the right to nominate more members of appropriate seniority and 
rank in the committee to conduct such enquiries to ensure equal representation of the gender 
as that of the complainant or for any other valid reason. The Complaints Committee is 
responsible for:  
• Investigating every formal written complaint of sexual harassment  
• Taking appropriate remedial measures to respond to any substantiated allegations of 
sexual harassment. 
• Discouraging and preventing employment-related sexual harassment 
f) Workplace Free from Violence 
The Organization will not tolerate workplace violence in any form either within premises or 
outside where company related activities are carried out. Employees are expected to not 
indulge in workplace violence. They must not encourage others towards it as well. Employees 
are also prohibited from possessing weapons or dangerous items at workplace or outside while 
conducting business activities. 
g) Open Door Communication 
The Organization believes that the work environment should be free from any kind of bureaucracy 
and all employees must have access to other employees regardless of their position or influence in 
the company. All managers are expected to foster an open-door culture at the workplace. 
 
  
 
h) Prohibition of child labor  
The Organization strictly prohibits the employment of child labor at its premises. All employees who 
are responsible for hiring are required to ensure that this principle is upheld. 
i) Environmental, Health & Safety 
The Organization is committed to provide its employees a safe, healthy, and ergonomically sound 
working environment. The company will take all possible measures to ensure health and safety of 
its employees. Safety at workplace is also every employee's responsibility. All employees and 
visitors to the workplace must comply with safety norms/policies/standards as prescribed by the 
company and applicable law. All employees must ensure that no unsafe act is committed at 
workplace. Employees must also undertake all possible measures to eliminate any unsafe 
condition as soon as they become aware of it. If an employee witnesses any unsafe act or unsafe 
condition, they should report to relevant authorities at the earliest. 
j) Human Rights 
The Organization recognizes the importance of maintaining and promoting fundamental human 
rights in all our operations and throughout our values, codes and employment policies work 
together to support the principles of Human Rights. We operate under the program and policies 
that: -  
• Provide fair and equitable wages, benefits and other conditions of employment. 
• Are in accordance with local laws  
• Provide humane and safe working conditions 
• Prohibit all forms of forced and compulsory labor or child labor  
• Promote workplace free of discrimination and harassment   
k) Equal Opportunity for All 
The Organization gives equal opportunity to all and does not discriminate against any person 
because of their gender, caste, religion, age (within statutory limits), marital status, nationality, 
ancestry, ethnicity, geographical origin, sexual orientation, disability or any other trait protected 
by law, with respect to any terms of employment such as hiring, promotion, transfer, 
compensation & benefits, career development opportunities, etc. It is expected that managers 
shall take employment related decisions based only on the merit of the person and not 
discriminate against any person because of their personal characteristics/traits. 
 
 
  
 
l) Code of Personal conduct 
• All employees are expected to demonstrate the highest standards of honesty and integrity 
in their conduct at all time while representing the Company and conducting business on 
behalf of the Company. 
• All employees are expected to demonstrate respect and trustworthy behavior in their 
dealings with other employees as well as external stakeholder. 
• All employees are expected to uphold the spirit of teamwork and ensure that the best 
interest of the team and Company always prevails. 
• All employees are expected to maintain a drug-free environment at workplace and refrain 
from substance abuse of any form while performing your duty within premises or outside of 
it. Employees are also prohibited from selling, distributing, possessing or encouraging 
others to use controlled substances. 
m) Drugs and Alcohol 
The abuse of drugs and alcohol can threaten the safety of the employees and have an adverse 
effect on job performance and Company’s reputation. The Organization will not tolerate any 
employee being under the influence of drugs or alcohol while performing his job, including but 
not limited to driving on business. Employees who violate our drug and alcohol policy may be 
subject to potential criminal liability as well as appropriate disciplinary action, including 
termination of employment. 
VI. Protection of Company Property 
All employees should treat our company’s property, whether material or intangible, with respect and 
care. 
Employees:  
 Should not misuse company equipment or use it frivolously. 
 Should respect all kinds of incorporeal property. This includes trademarks, copyright and other 
property (information, reports etc.) Employees should use them only to complete their job duties. 
 Employees should protect company facilities and other material property from damage and 
vandalism, whenever possible. 
a) Company Confidential Information 
For the Company, confidential information is a valuable asset, and every director, employee and agent 
of the Company must protect it. Confidential information includes all non-public information. It also 
includes personal information (regardless of its source) that all obtain during business. The employees 
must take care that all confidential information is used for Company business purposes only and in 
case of personal information, in addition, it must be processed on instructions from the Company in 
  
 
accordance with laid out policies, procedures and guidelines and as per applicable privacy laws and 
regulations. 
b) Accuracy of Record 
It is crucial that the Organization maintains accurate records and internal control systems. As such, 
the employees must record all transactions and prepare accurate and complete records, in 
accordance with established procedures. The employees must not inaccurately record time for 
reporting purposes, provide false or intentionally misleading information to the Organization, submit 
false or misleading claims or falsify any official the Company documents. Such actions could result in 
disciplinary actions. 
c) Intellectual Property & Publications 
The intellectual property of the Company must be protected as a vital business asset. Our intellectual 
property portfolio includes copyrights, patents, trademarks, service marks, trade secrets, design 
rights, logos, brands and know-how. We must focus on protecting these assets. It is important to 
ensure that to the extent permitted by law, the rights to all intellectual properties created using the 
Company’s time and expense that which are within the scope of our duties are assigned to and are the 
property of the Company. The Company/employee should promptly disclose any works, inventions or 
developments that are created to obtain legal protection over them. 
d) Use of Company Assets 
The use of the Company assets for individual profit or any unlawful, unauthorized personal or unethical 
purpose is prohibited. The Company’s information technology, intellectual property (e.g., copyrights, 
patents, and trademarks), facilities, equipment, machines, software, and cash may be used for 
business purposes only, including responsible and accurate expense reimbursement, and in 
accordance with applicable policies. 
Other assets (e.g., computers, printers, and copiers) may be used for minor and incidental personal 
purposes provided such use is kept to a minimum, and does not create any significant incremental 
costs, interfere with work duties, or violate any laws or Company policies. The use of any Company 
resources for personal political activities is prohibited.   
Computer hardware, software, data, and facilities are valuable resources that need protection from 
potential destruction, theft, or misuse. These resources may also include confidential client or 
Company information that requires safeguarding. It is employee’s responsibility to prevent 
unauthorized access using ID badges, passwords, or other security codes, and physical security 
measures (such as using computer cable locks, not leaving computers unattended in cars, and other 
normal precautions). Copyrighted materials (e.g., books, music, software, and magazines) should not 
be reproduced, distributed, or altered without permission of the copyright owner or an authorized 
agent. Software used in connection with the business of the Company should be properly licensed and 
used only in accordance with that license. Using unlicensed software could constitute copyright 
infringement and may be grounds for disciplinary action.  
  
 
e) Social Media Usage 
The Organization expects the employees to comply with applicable laws and government guidelines 
governing social media. When using any form of social media, one must comply with this Code of 
Conduct. The employees must not disclose any confidential information about the Company or any of 
its employees, contractors or third-party vendors. The Organization do not encourage sharing and being 
part of any political or social propaganda on behalf of the Company unless specifically asked to do so. 
f) Data Security 
The Organization maintains sensitive data and other information which is valuable to the functioning of 
its business. It is imperative that such information does not end up in the wrong hands. Thus, only 
employees who have a need to use confidential data or sensitive information will have access to it. 
Whenever the Organization receives a request to disclose potentially sensitive or confidential 
information such disclosure must be both appropriate and legally necessary. 
VII. Anti-Bribery & Corruption 
The Organization follows zero tolerance policy on bribery and corruption or other facilitation 
payments in any form whether in government or non-government dealings. The company prefers 
forgoing business opportunities rather than paying bribes. Employees accepting gifts from clients 
or partners is not appreciated. The Organization prohibit briberies for the benefit of any external or 
internal party. 
VIII. Conflict of Interest 
When the interests or benefits of one person conflict with the interests or benefits of the Company, 
a conflict of interest is said to occur. The Employees must avoid situations involving actual or 
potential conflict of interest so that even the slightest doubt about the company’s integrity is not 
raised. Conflicts of interest also occur when the employee or their family members receive 
improper personal benefits, or preferential treatment as a result of our position, or the position of a 
family member, in the Company. Remember that such situations might impact our judgment or 
responsibilities towards the Company and the shareholders and customers. 
This Code of Conduct is not exhaustive and lays down only the general principles to be followed by 
all pares as covered under the code. The company may have separate codes/policies formulated 
for regulating various matters that may be required under the specific laws. The parties shall be 
responsible for adhering to such additional codes/policies as may be applicable to them.

Asset  Management  Policy  
1.  Purpose   
The  purpose  of  this  Asset  Management  Policy  is  to  establish  clear  guidelines  and  procedures  for  managing  
and
 
safeguarding
 
the
 
physical
 
and
 
digital
 
assets
 
of
 
the
 
organization.
 
This
 
policy
 
aims
 
to
 
ensure
 
that
 
assets
 
are
 
acquired,
 
used,
 
maintained,
 
and
 
disposed
 
of
 
in
 
an
 
efficient,
 
cost-effective,
 
and
 
secure
 
manner,
 
while
 
complying
 
with
 
legal
 
and
 
regulatory
 
requirements.
 
2.  Scope   
This  policy  applies  to  all  physical  and  digital  assets  owned,  leased,  or  otherwise  controlled  by  the  
organization.
 
This
 
includes
 
assets
 
used
 
by
 
employees,
 
contractors,
 
and
 
third
 
parties
 
who
 
may
 
have
 
access
 
to
 
company
 
assets.
 
3.  Asset  Classification   
To  ensure  that  assets  are  managed  effectively,  they  will  be  classified  into  the  following  categories:  
3.1.  Physical  Assets:  
●  Office  Equipment:  Computers,  printers,  mobile  devices,  servers,  office  furniture,  etc.  ●  Network  Infrastructure:  Routers,  switches,  firewalls,  network  cables,  wireless  access  points,  etc.  ●  Tools  and  Software:  Development  tools,  licenses,  and  any  other  hardware  or  software  used  for  
operational
 
or
 
project
 
purposes.
 ●  Vehicles  (if  applicable):  Any  vehicles  owned  or  leased  by  the  organization  for  business  purposes.  
3.2.  Digital  Assets:  
●  Intellectual  Property  (IP):  Software  code,  design  documents,  proprietary  algorithms,  patents,  
trademarks,
 
copyrights,
 
etc.
 ●  Data  and  Databases:  Databases,  backups,  customer  data,  financial  records,  and  any  other  digital  
information
 
critical
 
to
 
business
 
operations.
 ●  Licenses  and  Subscriptions:  Software  licenses,  cloud  services,  external  tools,  and  other  digital  
service
 
subscriptions.
 ●  Emails  and  Accounts:  Corporate  email  accounts,  project  management  tools,  cloud  storage  
accounts,
 
and
 
any
 
other
 
accounts
 
used
 
for
 
business
 
purposes.
 
4.  Asset  Acquisition  and  Allocation  
●  Approval  Process:  All  asset  acquisitions  (whether  physical  or  digital)  must  be  approved  by  the  
designated
 
department
 
head
 
and
 
the
 
finance
 
department.
 
A
 
formal
 
request
 
should
 
be
 
submitted
 
and
 
evaluated
 
based
 
on
 
necessity
 
and
 
budget
 
availability.
 ●  Asset  Register:  Once  an  asset  is  acquired,  it  must  be  recorded  in  the  company’s  Asset  Register.  
The
 
asset
 
register
 
will
 
include
 
details
 
such
 
as
 
asset
 
description,
 
category,
 
serial
 
number,
 
purchase
 
date,
 
location,
 
assigned
 
user,
 
and
 
expected
 
lifecycle.
 ●  Allocation  and  Assignment:  All  assets  must  be  allocated  and  assigned  to  specific  users  or  
departments.
 
An
 
asset
 
custodian
 
(usually
 
the
 
department
 
head
 
or
 
manager)
 
will
 
be
 
responsible
 
for

5.  Asset  Usage  and  Security  
●  Authorized  Use:  Assets  must  only  be  used  for  business-related  purposes.  Any  personal  use  of  
company
 
assets
 
(e.g.,
 
mobile
 
phones,
 
laptops)
 
must
 
be
 
explicitly
 
authorized
 
by
 
management.
 ●  Security  Measures:  All  assets  must  be  protected  from  theft,  damage,  and  unauthorized  access.  
Employees
 
must
 
follow
 
the
 
organization's
 
security
 
protocols,
 
such
 
as
 
setting
 
up
 
strong
 
passwords,
 
enabling
 
encryption,
 
and
 
ensuring
 
physical
 
security
 
(e.g.,
 
locking
 
devices
 
when
 
not
 
in
 
use).
 ●  Data  Security:  Digital  assets  containing  sensitive  or  proprietary  data  (e.g.,  customer  information,  
source
 
code,
 
etc.)
 
must
 
be
 
secured
 
with
 
encryption,
 
multi-factor
 
authentication
 
(MFA),
 
and
 
other
 
relevant
 
security
 
controls.
 ●  Tracking  and  Monitoring:  The  IT  department  will  periodically  monitor  and  track  the  location  and  
condition
 
of
 
high-value
 
or
 
sensitive
 
assets.
 
This
 
will
 
include
 
using
 
asset
 
management
 
software
 
or
 
a
 
manual
 
log,
 
where
 
applicable.
 
6.  Maintenance  and  Lifecycle  Management  
●  Regular  Maintenance:  Assets,  especially  physical  ones  like  servers,  workstations,  and  mobile  
devices,
 
must
 
undergo
 
regular
 
maintenance
 
and
 
software
 
updates
 
to
 
ensure
 
optimal
 
performance
 
and
 
security.
 ●  Warranty  and  Support:  The  organization  will  maintain  a  record  of  warranties,  service  contracts,  and  
support
 
agreements
 
for
 
each
 
asset
 
to
 
ensure
 
timely
 
maintenance
 
and
 
replacement
 
when
 
necessary.
 ●  Depreciation  and  Amortization:  Assets  will  be  depreciated  according  to  their  expected  useful  life  
and
 
in
 
accordance
 
with
 
relevant
 
accounting
 
standards.
 ●  Asset  Lifespan:  Each  asset  will  have  an  assigned  expected  useful  life.  At  the  end  of  its  lifespan,  the  
asset
 
should
 
either
 
be
 
replaced,
 
retired,
 
or
 
disposed
 
of
 
in
 
accordance
 
with
 
the
 
organization's
 
disposal
 
policy.
 
7.  Asset  Disposal  
●  Retirement  Process:  When  an  asset  reaches  the  end  of  its  lifecycle  or  is  no  longer  needed,  it  must  
be
 
retired
 
through
 
a
 
formal
 
process.
 
This
 
includes
 
ensuring
 
that
 
all
 
data
 
and
 
intellectual
 
property
 
are
 
securely
 
deleted
 
and
 
that
 
the
 
asset
 
is
 
disposed
 
of
 
in
 
an
 
environmentally
 
responsible
 
manner.
 ●  Data  Wiping:  Before  the  disposal  of  any  digital  asset  (e.g.,  computers,  mobile  devices,  or  storage  
media),
 
all
 
data
 
must
 
be
 
wiped
 
using
 
industry-standard
 
data
 
erasure
 
methods
 
to
 
prevent
 
data
 
recovery.
 ●  Disposal  Methods:  Physical  assets  (e.g.,  old  computers,  printers)  must  be  disposed  of  by  certified  
e-waste
 
management
 
vendors
 
or
 
through
 
donation,
 
recycling,
 
or
 
sale
 
as
 
per
 
organizational
 
guidelines.
 ●  Documentation  of  Disposal:  All  asset  disposals  must  be  documented,  including  the  asset  ID,  date  of  
disposal,
 
method
 
of
 
disposal,
 
and
 
confirmation
 
of
 
data
 
wiping
 
(if
 
applicable).
 
8.  Asset  Auditing  and  Compliance  
●  Regular  Audits:  The  organization  will  conduct  periodic  audits  of  physical  and  digital  assets  to  ensure  
that
 
the
 
inventory
 
matches
 
the
 
records
 
in
 
the
 
asset
 
register.
 
Any
 
discrepancies
 
will
 
be
 
investigated.
 ●  Compliance:  All  assets  and  asset  management  processes  will  comply  with  applicable  laws,  
regulations,
 
and
 
industry
 
standards
 
(e.g.,
 
IT
 
Act
 
2000,
 
GDPR,
 
ISO
 
27001,
 
etc.).
 ●  Internal  and  External  Audits:  The  organization  may  conduct  internal  audits  and  be  subject  to  
external
 
audits
 
to
 
verify
 
compliance
 
with
 
this
 
policy
 
and
 
ensure
 
that
 
asset
 
management
 
practices
 
are
 
being
 
followed.

4.  Change  Management  Process  
The  change  management  process  follows  a  structured  flow  from  request  initiation  to  
closure:
 
Step  1:  Change  Request  Submission  
●  Any  team  member  may  submit  a  change  request  (CR)  through  the  Change  
Request
 
System
 
or
 
ticketing
 
platform.
 ●  The  request  should  include  details  such  as  the  type  of  change,  reasons  for  the  
change,
 
potential
 
impacts,
 
and
 
proposed
 
timelines.
 
Step  2:  Change  Evaluation  &  Impact  Assessment  
●  The  Change  Advisory  Board  (CAB)  will  assess  the  change  based  on  its  potential  
impact,
 
risk,
 
cost,
 
and
 
resources
 
needed.
 ●  For  major  and  emergency  changes,  risk  assessments  will  be  conducted  to  
identify
 
possible
 
issues
 
that
 
may
 
arise.
 
Step  3:  Change  Approval  
●  All  standard  changes  should  be  pre-approved  as  part  of  the  standard  operating  
procedures.
 ●  Minor  changes  must  be  reviewed  and  approved  by  relevant  stakeholders  (e.g.,  
project
 
managers,
 
team
 
leads).
 ●  Major  and  emergency  changes  require  approval  from  the  CAB,  ensuring  senior  
management
 
and
 
stakeholders
 
are
 
informed.
 
Step  4:  Planning  and  Implementation  
●  Once  approved,  a  detailed  plan  will  be  created  that  outlines  the  timeline,  
resources,
 
and
 
steps
 
for
 
implementing
 
the
 
change.
 ●  Testing  and  validation  will  occur  in  a  controlled  environment  before  deployment  
to
 
ensure
 
minimal
 
disruption
 
to
 
production
 
systems.
 
Step  5:  Change  Implementation  
●  Implementation  is  carried  out  according  to  the  plan.  ●  If  the  change  is  a  major  or  emergency  change,  it  will  be  rolled  out  in  stages  or  
with
 
appropriate
 
rollback
 
procedures
 
in
 
place
 
to
 
avoid
 
system-wide
 
disruptions.

ID, Access Card and Locker Management Policy 
 
 
Objective 
To grant access to the Ideas2IT Technology Services Private Limited facility for authorized personnel 
only, to prevent loss and damage or to prevent compromise of physical assets including information in 
physical form and to minimize interruptions to business activities by implementing adequate physical 
access controls. 
Scope 
This is applicable to all across the Ideas2IT Technology Services Private Limited premises and all Employees 
in Ideas2IT. 
Eligibility 
Access Request for 
• All permanent employees 
• Contract employees 
• Vendors 
• Guest/Visitor 
Guidelines 
ID and Access card 
Employees and Contract Employees  
• Admin team shall be responsible to issue the ID and Access card to all the employees joining the 
organization.   
• ID card needs to be displayed prominently by all Ideas2IT Technology Services Technology 
Services Limited employees while in the office premises and shall not be given to any other 
person to gain entry into office premises. 
S. No Version Release Date Description of Change Created / Modified by Approved by 
 1 1.0   28-Sep-2022 Initial  Admin Team Arun Ganesan  
            
            
   
 
For Internal use only  
 Page | 1 
 
 
• Personnel with Worn-out/damaged ID card shall not be allowed entry into the facility. 
• Access cards are enabled with specific access rights based on a need to enter basis by the Admin 
team and are "Non-transferable".  
• Proxy swiping, tail gating and misuse of access rights is not allowed, any violations shall be 
reported to HR.  
• Employees will be provided access rights to their regular workplace only.  
• Only authorized employees will be allowed to enter restricted areas such as server room / ups 
room or any other place.  
• Employees who forget to bring ID card will be given a temporary card with access for the specific 
day. Please reach out to the ground floor security desk.  
• At the time of separation from the company, employee’s ID card and Access cards should be 
returned to the Admin team as part of the Exit Clearance Process. ID card will be destroyed, and 
access will be disabled.    
• On loss of ID/Access card employee should immediately inform the Admin team over an email. 
On receipt of information of loss of access card, the admin team shall ensure immediate 
revocation of all access rights to avoid any misuse.  
• Employee should raise a Service Request in iAssistant for a new ID and access card. 
• Loss of ID and access card will be issued on a chargeable basis. ID card INR 50 and Access card 
INR 150.     
Guest and Vendors 
• Any planned visits should be communicated by the host department in three working days 
advance through an e-mail to the Admin team. 
• On the day and time of meeting, guests should report at the reception desk to facilitate the 
entry to the facility. 
• At the reception desk, identity of the guest will be validated through a government issued photo 
identity card. In the case of domestic visitors- driver’s license, PAN card, Voter’s ID card, 
Passport, Aadhar card and in the case of foreign nationals- in addition to any of these, Business 
cards and individual’s company ID cards are not considered valid form of identity proof. 
• Guests’ baggage is liable to security check. 
• On arrival of host, guests are issued with visitor ID card which must be worn and displayed 
prominently. 
• The host should escort the guest during the entire duration of their visit. 
• Host is responsible to ensure that guest ID and access cards are returned to the security desk at 
the reception at the end of the visit. 
• Official guests visiting for more than a day will be managed on a daily basis for guest ID card 
issuance. However, if the duration of visit is over 15 days, the host may apply for a non-
employee ID badge. In this case an access card will also be issued and enabled as per the access 
control matrix. The host requesting for the ID badge and access card is responsible for return of 
   
 
For Internal use only  
 Page | 2 
 
 
the same to the Admin team. In case the access card is not returned the cost of the access cards 
has to be borne by the host. 
• Personal guests should not proceed to areas other than common areas such as cafeteria and 
ground floor lobby. 
Access to sensitive areas 
• Access shall be given to restricted area on based on the necessity and approval by authorized 
personnel. 
• Admin team will maintain list of sensitive areas in each location. 
List of Sensitive areas are 
• Server rooms, CCTV Room, UPS / Electrical Room 
• Any other area which will be declared as sensitive from time to time 
Unattended user equipment 
Any unused/unattended device being found by Admin team or handed over by an employee to Admin 
Team, it would be communicated and stored with Admin team for a period of one working day.  
 
Key Management 
• Original keys of Main doors and other lockable areas such as storeroom, UPS room, storage 
lockers etc. will be available with Admin team.  
• One set each of duplicate keys would be kept with admin team 
• Original keys should be issued to the authorized personnel or his representatives on need basis. 
Admin team will maintain list of authorized persons for withdrawal and deposition of keys.   
• In case of any emergency like fire, natural calamities, security should use the original keys to 
enter the area to control the situation. Concurrence of the authorize person to be taken at the 
earliest opportunity. Appropriate recording of such key movement must be maintained. 
• Keys should be labeled, and easily retrievable and key issue register will be maintained by admin 
team. 
• Loss of keys will be necessitated to change of locks by the admin team and cost will be borne by 
concerned user.  
Disclaimer 
The applicability, eligibility of the this policy may be implemented and/or changed by Ideas2IT 
Technology Service Private Limited from time to time at the sole discretion of Ideas2IT Technology 
Service Private Limited and such implemented and/or changed  shall  become applicable to the 
employees immediately, upon receipt of notice of the same.

Objective 
All employees of Ideas2IT Technology Services Private Limited shall support and ensure to protect the 
IT assets of the organization.  
Scope 
This document applies to all full time, part time and contract employees of the Ideas2IT Technology 
Services Private Limited and its subsidiaries. 
Definition  
IT asset means laptop/s, mouse, headphone, laptop charger, speaker, pen drive, headset, data card, 
hard disk, mobile, tablets, SIM card and any other IT assets/equipment’s provided to an employee  
to deliver his/her services at Ideas2IT until he/she is associated with the Company. 
Process 
• New Joiners- HR Team to inform the System Admin Team on the new joiner details seven 
business days before the date of joining to get the required assets (Laptop, Laptop Bag & 
Laptop Charger) ready along with the e-mail id creation. 
• Employees- Employee to send a request email to System Admin team along with manager’s 
approval while requesting for Data card, headset, or any other assets. 
• All the assets provided by the organization to the employee shou ld be returned as in the 
condition while it was provided while exiting. The failure to do so, will lead to the appropriate 
amount being deducted from your salary while processing full and final settlement.   
Policy Guidelines  
It is Ideas2IT Technology Services Private Limited’s policy that the employee shall be fully responsible 
for lost, stolen, broken or damaged  IT asset/equipment that has been issued to an employee to be 
used during his/ her employment with Ideas2IT Technology Services Private Limited. 
a) Case of damage/broken asset: 
• Employees shall inform System Admin  about the damaged/broken asset immediately 
(within 1 business day) at systemadmin@ideas2it.com, marking copy to his/her reporting 
manager. 
 
Internal 
 2 
• Employees are responsible for proper care of IT Assets issued, including repair or 
replacement of IT assets damaged as a result of negligent use. 
• Employees must provide adequate security to the asset and return the asset in the same 
condition as it was before usage. 
 
b) Case of stolen/loss of asset: 
• Employees shall inform system admin team, the reporting manager and HR team about the 
lost/ stolen asset immediately (within 1 business day) at systemadmin@ideas2it.com and 
hr@ideas2it.com. 
 
• Employees shall file an FIR in the nearby Police station and obtain a copy of FIR, which shall 
be submitted to the System Admin team and the HR team within 2 business days. 
 
• The System Admin department shall immediately freeze all communication to the lost/ stolen 
IT asset. 
 
c) Recovery of Amount in case of damage/broken/loss/stolen  
• Employees have to bear the expenses towards broken/damaged assets at actuals and in the 
case of theft/stolen, the recovery of cost will be decided at the sole discretion of the 
management. 
• Screen/Physical/Liquid damage – Screen/Physical/Liquid damage will not get covered under 
warranty, hence in such cases the employee shall bear the cost of repair at actual. 
 
• The recovery amount can be transferred to Ideas2IT Technology Services Private Limited bank 
account or can be recovered through the monthly payroll of the employee.   
 
Other asset – docking station, pen drive, hard disc, data card, laptop charger/ bag/mouse, 
headset, mobile phone, etc. (assets mentioned above but not limited to)  
• The amount would be determined by the System Admin team based on asset value, date of 
purchase, etc. 
Laptop Security Best Practices: 
Physical Security: 
• An employee shall ensure the safety and security of the laptop and should never be left 
unattended in any location.  
• An employee shall never leave the laptop on the work desk overnight  and the Company will 
not take the responsibility if the asset is stolen/theft. 
 
 
 
 
Internal 
 3 
Technical Security: 
• The System Admin team protects the laptop with hard drive encryption. 
• Encryption is vital for making sure data on the laptop doesn't fall into the wrong hands in case 
the laptop is lost or stolen. 
• Full disk encryption makes the laptop unusable to anyone to avoid data theft. Even if the disk 
is foisted out of the machine and installed on a test bed, the data is gibberish. 
• An employee shall always lock the laptop while being away always! 
• Save important work-related files to your cloud (Google Drive).  
 
Enforcement:  
Since data security and integrity along with asset protection is critical to the operations of Ideas2IT, 
employees who do not adhere to this policy shall be subject to disciplinary action up to and including 
keep them educated about the latest techniques and methods of IT asset policy. 
 
Disclaimer: 
The applicability, eligibility of the Asset Policy may be implemented and/or changed by the 
management of Ideas2IT from time to time at the sole discretion of management of Ideas2IT and such 
implemented and/or changed shall become applicable to the employees immediately, upon receipt 
of notice of the same.

1.  Purpose 
This Leave Policy is designed to establish a structured, transparent, and sustainable leave 
framework. The policy aims to balance employee well-being with operational continuity 
while standardizing leave accrual, utilization, accumulation, and encashment practices 
across the organization. 
2. Policy Scope 
This policy sets out the various types of leave that an employee is eligible for and outlines 
the procedure for availing leave. Leave entitlements are calculated on a calendar year 
basis (1st January to 31st December). 
3. Annual Leave Entitlement (Total: 24 Days) 
 Casual Leave (CL): 6 days per calendar year 
 Sick Leave (SL): 6 days per calendar year 
 Earned Leave (EL): 12 days per calendar year 
 EL Accumulation Cap: Maximum 20 days 
 Leave Credit Cycle: Quarterly (6 days per quarter) 
 
 
Leave Category Quarterly Credit Leave Credit Status 
Casual Leave (CL) 1.5 days Credited at the beginning of each Quarter 
Sick Leave (SL) 1.5 days Credited at the beginning of each Quarter 
Earned Leave (EL) 3 days Credited at the beginning of each Quarter 
4. Types of Leave and Entitlements 
 
4.1 Casual Leave (CL) 
 Employees are entitled to 6 days of Casual Leave per calendar year. 
 CL is intended for short-term or unforeseen personal requirements. 
 Casual Leave (CL) cannot be carried forward to the next calendar year or encashed. 
 Unutilized CL will lapse at the end of the calendar year. 
4.2 Sick Leave (SL) 
 Employees are entitled to 6 days of Sick Leave per calendar year. 
 SL is applicable in case of illness or medical emergency. 
 Sick leave (SL) cannot be carried forward to the next calendar year or encashed. 
 Unutilized SL will lapse at the end of the calendar year. 
4.3 Earned Leave (EL) 
 Employees are entitled to 12 days of Earned Leave (EL) per calendar year. 
 EL is credited quarterly at the beginning of each quarter. 
 Up to 8 days of unused EL will be carried forward to the next calendar year. 
 EL can be accumulated up to a maximum of 20 days. 
 EL may be utilized for planned or long-term leave requirements. 
(Note: Employees can avail leave in any order as per their preference, subject to 
approval and applicable policy guidelines.) 
 
 
 
5. Earned Leave (EL) Encashment Policy 
 Out of the total 12 EL credited annually, a maximum of 8 days per calendar year 
is eligible for encashment. 
 Employees may apply for Earned Leave (EL) encashment on a quarterly basis.  
 Employees may encash EL partially or fully, as per their requirement (for 
example, if 10 days are encashed, the remaining balance will continue in the EL 
account). 
 EL encashment will be calculated based on the employee’s Basic Pay. 
 EL encashment is permitted only once in a calendar year. 
 The EL balance must not exceed the accumulation cap of 20 days. 
 Any Earned Leave (EL) balance exceeding 20 days will lapse. 
 EL encashment will be processed through payroll, and applicable statutory 
taxes will be deducted. 
 EL encashment is applicable only to active employees. 
 Employees serving their notice period or who have resigned are not eligible for 
EL encashment. 
 The remaining EL balance after encashment will continue in the employee’s EL 
account. 
Note: Employees who are serving their resignation notice period are not eligible to 
avail Casual Leave (CL), Sick Leave (SL), Privilege Leave (PL) (if any), Earned Leave 
(EL), and Work from Home (WFH). 
 
5.1 PL to EL Conversion Logic 
As part of the policy transition, existing Privilege Leave (PL) balances were reviewed 
and aligned under the new leave structure. This was a one-time exercise to convert 
eligible PL into Earned Leave (EL) for employees holding PL balances. 
Employees who had Privilege Leave (PL) were given the option either to convert their 
PL into Earned Leave (EL) or to continue with their existing PL balance. This 
conversion was optional and applicable only once, effective from the 
implementation date of the revised policy. 
Based on the responses received from employees, the conversion has been 
processed accordingly. For employees who opted not to convert, their PL balance 
will continue to remain as Privilege Leave (PL) under the existing structure. 
 
 
 
 
Conversion Logic 
Case 1: If PL Balance ≤ 6 Days 
 If an employee’s PL balance is less than or equal to 6 days, 
→ The PL balance will remain unchanged in the PL account. 
 No transfer to EL will occur. 
 
 Case 2: If PL Balance Exceeds 6 Days 
• If an employee’s Privilege Leave (PL) balance exceeds 6 days, the following conversion 
logic shall apply: 
1. Standard Deduction: 
Six (6) or seven (7) days will be retained from the existing PL balance, depending on 
whether the current balance is an even or odd number.  
Eg: 1.1 Current PL balance is an even number: If your current PL balance in 10,  
you will be eligible for 6 days standard deduction. 
        1.2 Current PL balance is an odd number: If your current PL balance is 11, you 
will be eligible for 7 days standard deduction.  
2. Conversion to Earned Leave (EL): 
After the applicable standard deduction, the remaining Privilege Leave (PL) balance 
shall be converted into Earned Leave (EL) in the ratio 2:1 and credited to the 
employee’s EL account. The standard retained balance of six (6) or seven (7) days 
will continue to remain in the PL account and can be used until fully exhausted, with 
no expiry. 
For Eg: If your PL as on date is 10 days, 6 days (standard deduction will be applied) and you 
will continue to have 6 days in PL and the remaining 4 days will be converted to 2 days EL. 
If your PL as on date is 11 days, 7 days (standard deduction will be applied) and you will 
continue to have 7 days in PL and the remaining 4 days will be converted to 2 days EL. 
 
 
 
 
 
7.2 PL to EL Conversion – Calculation Examples 
Example 1 (Even Number) 
• PL Balance: 10 days 
• Deducted from PL: 6 days 
• Remaining PL: 4 days 
• EL credited = In the ratio 2 PL :1 EL = 2 EL days 
Final Outcome: 
– PL Balance: 6 
– Additional Credit to EL: 2 days 
Example 2 (Odd Number) 
• PL Balance: 13 days 
• Deducted from PL: 7 days 
• Remaining PL: 6 days 
• EL credited = In the ratio 2 PL :1 EL = 3 EL days 
Final Outcome: 
– PL Balance: 7 
– Additional Credit to EL: 3 days 
Example 3 (Less than or equal to 6 days) 
• PL Balance: 6 days 
• Since PL ≤ 6 
• No conversion applied 
Final Outcome: 
– PL Balance: 6 days 
– Additional Credit to EL: Zero (No conversion of EL to PL) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
6. Additional Leave Categories 
The following leave categories are governed by statutory requirements and the company’s 
internal policies. These leaves are over and above the annual leave entitlement and do not 
form part of CL or EL balances. 
6.1 Maternity Leave 
a. In Case of Pregnancy 
1. Maternity Leave benefits are governed by Indian labour laws, including the Maternity 
Benefit Act, 1961, and applicable amendments. 
2. Employees become eligible for Maternity Leave after completing 80 days of 
confirmed employment with Ideas2IT. 
3. Eligible employees are entitled to 26 weeks of paid Maternity Leave for the first and 
second child, as per company records. 
4. For the third or subsequent child, employees are entitled to 12 weeks of paid 
Maternity Leave. 
5. Maternity Leave may be split before and after delivery—up to 8 weeks before the 
expected delivery date, with the remaining period after childbirth. 
6. A medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner stating the expected 
date of delivery must be submitted along with the leave request. 
7. Employees wishing to extend leave beyond the entitled Maternity Leave period may 
apply for unpaid special leave after exhausting their Privilege Leave (PL). The total 
period of absence, including Maternity Leave and extended leave, shall not exceed 
eight months. Upon return, the employee will be reinstated to the same position 
held prior to Maternity Leave. 
8. Any extension beyond the statutory Maternity Leave period is subject to 
management discretion. 
9. Any extension beyond the statutory Maternity Leave period shall first be adjusted 
against the employee’s available leave balance. Once all eligible leave balances are 
exhausted, the remaining period of absence will be treated as Leave Without Pay 
(LWP). 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
b. In Case of Adoption 
1. Maternity Leave provisions for adopting mothers are governed by Indian labour 
laws. 
2. Maternity Leave for adopting mothers is applicable only if the adopted child is below 
three months of age. 
3. Eligible adopting mothers are entitled to 12 weeks of paid Maternity Leave, 
commencing from the date of adoption. 
4. Extension of leave beyond the entitled period may be requested as unpaid special 
leave after exhausting PL, subject to the maximum absence period of eight months. 
5. All extensions are subject to management approval. 
 
6.2 Paternity Leave 
1. Paternity Leave is applicable for the birth or adoption of the first and second child 
only, as per company records. 
2. Eligible employees are entitled to 5 days of Paternity Leave per delivery or adoption. 
3. Leave requests must be supported with valid documentation (medical or adoption-
related) and approved in advance by the reporting manager. 
4. Paternity Leave may be availed: 
 Within four weeks before or after the spouse’s delivery, or 
 Within four weeks of the adoption of a child. Any Paternity Leave not availed 
within this period will be considered forfeited. 
 
7. General Leave Rules & Administration 
7.1 Leave Application & Approval 
All leave requests must be submitted through iAssistant and approved in advance 
by the reporting manager. 
Path: iAssistant → Leave Request → Apply Leave Request 
7.2 Unapproved Absence / Leave Without Pay (LWP) 
Any leave of absence not applied for or approved in iAssistant will be treated as 
Leave Without Pay (LWP). 
Additionally, if an employee neither submits a Leave/Work from Home request in 
iAssistant nor has an official access entry recorded for the day, the absence will be 
considered LWP. 
 
 
7.3 Holidays and Weekly Offs During Leave 
If a declared public holiday or weekly off falls within an approved leave period, such 
day(s) shall not be counted as leave. 
 
8. Policy Amendments & Review 
Management reserves the right to amend, modify, suspend, or withdraw any part of this 
policy at its discretion, in accordance with applicable statutory requirements and 
organizational needs. This policy will be reviewed annually or as required by HR. 
Disclaimer 
The applicability and eligibility of this Leave Policy may be implemented and/or modified by 
Ideas2IT from time to time at its sole discretion. Any such changes shall become effective 
immediately upon communication to employees. 
 
 
Leave Policy – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 
1. What is the total number of leaves I am entitled to in a year? 
You are entitled to 24 days of paid leave per calendar year, comprising: 
 6 days of Casual Leave (CL) 
 6 days of Sick Leave (SL) 
 12 days of Earned Leave (EL) 
 
2. What is the leave year followed by the company? 
The leave year follows the calendar year, from 1st January to 31st December. 
3. How and when are leaves credited? 
Leaves are credited quarterly at the beginning of each quarter as follows: 
 Casual Leave (CL): 1.5 days per quarter 
 Sick Leave (SL): 1.5 days per quarter 
 Earned Leave (EL): 3 days per quarter 
Total quarterly credit: 6 days 
 
 
4. Can I carry forward my unused Casual Leave (CL)? 
No. Casual Leave cannot be carried forward or encashed. Any unused CL will lapse at the 
end of the calendar year. 
5. Can I carry forward my unused Sick Leave (SL)? 
No. Sick Leave cannot be carried forward or encashed. Any unused SL will lapse at the end 
of the calendar year. 
6. Can Earned Leave (EL) be carried forward? 
Yes. Only up to 8 days of unused EL can be carried forward to the next calendar year. 
7. What is the maximum EL balance I can maintain? 
Earned Leave can be accumulated up to a maximum of 20 days. Any balance exceeding 20 
days will lapse. 
8. Am I eligible for Earned Leave (EL) encashment? 
Yes. Employees may encash Earned Leave, subject to the following: 
 Once you have reached 20 days in your EL account, you are eligible for 
encashment. 
 Encashment can be availed once in a calendar year. 
 EL encashment is processed through payroll and subject to statutory tax 
deductions. 
 
9. How is EL encashment paid? 
EL encashment is: 
 Processed through payroll 
 Subject to applicable statutory tax deductions 
 
10. In what order should leaves be utilized? 
Employees may avail leave in any order based on their needs, subject to manager approval 
and policy guidelines. 
 
 
 
11. What happens to my existing Privilege Leave (PL)? 
Your existing PL balance will be transitioned in accordance with the PL-to-EL conversion 
logic defined in the policy, or it may remain in your PL account without any expiry period. 
12. What if my PL balance is 6 days or less? 
 Your PL balance will remain unchanged. 
 No conversion to EL will take place. 
13. What if my PL balance exceeds 6 days? 
If your PL balance exceeds six (6) days: 
 Six (6) days (for even balance) or seven (7) days (for odd balance) will be retained in 
PL. 
 The remaining balance will be converted to EL in the ratio of 2 PL : 1 EL. 
 The retained PL balance will remain available until fully utilized. 
 
14. How is an odd PL balance handled during conversion? 
If the PL balance is an odd number, 7 days will remain in PL and the remaining balance will 
be converted to EL in the ratio of 2:1. 
15. How do I apply for leave? 
All leave requests must be submitted through iAssistant: 
Path: iAssistant → Leave Request → Apply Leave Request 
Leave must be approved by your reporting manager. 
 
16. What happens if I do not apply for leave in iAssistant? 
Any absence without an approved leave or WFH request will be treated as Leave Without 
Pay (LWP). 
17. What will happen to my final PL balance after conversion? 
After conversion, the retained 6 or 7 PL days will remain in your PL account until fully 
exhausted. 
 
 
 
 
18. What if I neither apply for leave nor have an access entry? 
If there is: 
 No leave/WFH request, and 
 No official access entry recorded 
the absence will be treated as LOP. 
 
19. Are holidays and weekly offs counted as leave? 
No. If a public holiday or a weekly off falls during an approved leave period, it will not be 
counted as leave. 
20. Am I eligible to encash Earned Leave during my notice period or at exit? 
No. Employees serving notice period or who have submitted resignation are not eligible for 
EL encashment, including at the time of exit.

Introduction and Objective 
 
To provide employees with financial assistance in certain emergency situations when a salary advance 
is not sufficient to cover emergency financial requirements of an employee 
 
Applicability 
 
The policy applies to all permanent employees. This policy is also applicable to all employees active 
on the rolls. All employees of Ideas2IT will be bound by this policy. This policy is applicable for availing 
staff loan/salary advance during the association with Ideas2IT with effect from 1st August 2022. 
 
Policy Guidelines 
 
Eligibility Criteria:  
 
• Loans will be granted to all employees, whose employment has been confirmed and 
completed a minimum of one year as on the date of loan application.  
• New loan will be sanctioned only after 100% repayment of the previous loan and there must 
be a 3 months gap before availing the next loan. Besides, employees can avail up to a 
maximum of only 1 loan within a financial year.  
• Loans will be granted in the following instances and at the sole discretion of the management.  
o Medical Emergencies for Self/Spouse/Parents/Siblings/Children 
o Child Education

• The maximum eligible loan amount shall be INR 2 Lakhs and will be decided at the sole 
discretion of the management. 
• Loan recovery will be a maximum period of 12 EMI’s (12 months). This will be intimated to the 
employee at the time of approval. Any installments which are greater than 12 months shall 
attract an interest at the rate of 10.25%, which will be deducted from the salary along with 
the EMI and the employee has to sign the promissory note in view of the statutory 
requirements. The interest rate shall be reviewed by finance team on quarterly basis 
depending upon the changes in the bank rates.  
• The repayment will be done by deducting the EMI’s from the salary every month 
subsequently. For instance, if loan is disbursed in Month 1, deduction will start from Month 
2. Cooling period for repayment of loan can be provided to a maximum of 3 months provided 
the repayment of loan happens within 12 months from the date of disbursement. 
• The employees can close the loan by paying the entire outstanding during any time of the

Purpose: 
The purpose of the Work from Home policy is to establish guidelines and expectations for 
employees who work remotely, typically from their homes. The policy outlines the requirements 
and responsibilities of an employee and sets clear expectations for communication, productivity, 
security, and performance. Work-from-home arrangements can be occasional or temporary. 
Eligibility 
Employees under full-time employment are entitled to the work-from-home (WFH) 
option, except for the following: 
 
1. WFH or hybrid work arrangements will not be applicable during critical business 
situations, including but not limited to: 
a. Client escalations or emergencies. 
b. Projects designated as "red" or high-risk. 
c. Situations where critical deliverables are due and require close coordination. 
d. Any other circumstance where in-office presence is deemed essential by 
management. 
These exceptions take precedence, and employees must comply with the requirement to 
be physically present at the workplace as needed. 
2. Employees currently in training/upskilling. 
3. Employees with 0 to 1 year of experience are not eligible for work -from-home (WFH) or 
hybrid work arrangements. Employees with 1 to 2 years of experience are also not eligible 
for WFH or hybrid mode. However, employees who demonstrate exceptional

4. Senior leadership and due to the nature of their roles, are generally expected to work from

5. Support team members are typically required to work from the office to ensure effective

physical presence to maintain smooth operations and provide timely assistance. 
WFH Days 
1. Mandatory WFH Day: Each project team is allowed to work from home for two days per 
week, totaling up to eight days per month. The Project Manager will determine this day 
based on project requirements and team dynamics. This cannot be carried forward to the 
following week or month. 
2. Any additional WFH days beyond the allowed eight per month will be deducted from the 
employee's Casual Leave (CL), Privilege Leave (PL), or treated as Leave Without Pay 
(LOP) if no leave balance is available. 
3. If an employee decides to work from the office on their designated work-from-home days, 
these days cannot be compensated or exchanged for additional time off. 
Criteria for WFH Approval 
1. Work Schedule: Employees must adhere to their regular work hours and be available 
during core hours. 
2. Communication/Availability: Employees must be reachable via email, phone, and 
instant messaging during working hours. 
3. Productivity: Employees are expected to maintain the same level of productivity and 
meet all deadlines as if they were working in the office. 
4. Workspace: Employees must ensure a suitable and secure workspace at home, free from 
distractions and with a reliable internet connection. 
Responsibilities 
1. Employee Responsibilities: 
○ Ensure they have access to the necessary tools and resources to perform their 
duties effectively. 
○ Comply with all company policies and guidelines while working from home. 
○ Report any technical issues immediately to the IT department. 
 
2. Manager Responsibilities: 
○ Ensure fair and consistent application of the WFH policy. 
○ Monitor and evaluate the productivity of employees working from home.
